To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) GPs are not well prepared to educate patients about the nature of depression and anxiety, 2) GPs have a poor understanding of the patient's perspective on the nature of the illness and its treatment, and 3) GPs are more likely to provide a patient-centered education when they perceive the consultation as a learning opportunity.
GPs are well positioned to provide a range of interventions for depression and anxiety in their patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the GP as an educator in the context of depression and anxiety, and the factors that affect the extent to which this role is fulfilled.
the role of social workers in mental health care, the social work profession's contribution to mental health policy and practice, and the social work profession itself.
